about: Research sheet for the North Dakota county edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files.
name: North Dakota
phones_sentence: County veterans service officer phones, addresses and hours come from each county’s page on the North Dakota Department of Veterans Affairs website. Many rural offices are open only certain days; call ahead.

offices.source_title: North Dakota Department of Veterans Affairs: Veteran Service Officers
offices.note: County veterans service officers help with VA claims, pension and survivor benefits at no charge.
offices.selection: Office address, phone and hours as printed on each county’s page on the department’s website, each read in full; officers’ names, emails, cell and home phones omitted. The Billings, Golden Valley, Grant, Hettinger and Mercer pages send veterans to the Stark County office in Dickinson. Slope’s page lists no office phone, so it shows the officer’s work phone. Phone extensions are in the notes. Renville’s mailing address is left out because its ZIP code does not match the town.

aging.source_title: North Dakota Health and Human Services: Adults and Aging Services
aging.source_scope: Aging and Disability Resource LINK, toll-free (855) 462-5465, Relay ND TTY 711; the Adults and Aging Services section, 1237 W. Divide Avenue, Suite 6, Bismarck; read in full. The page is undated. The 2023 Vulnerable Adult Protective Services handout gives option 1 for the Resource LINK (https://www.hhs.nd.gov/sites/www/files/documents/vaps-handout-2023.pdf; search excerpt). North Dakota has no Area Agencies on Aging; the state section runs Older Americans Act services statewide.
aging.description: The Aging & Disability Resource LINK, run statewide by North Dakota Health and Human Services: free information and referral on help at home, meals, caregiver support, assisted living and other long-term services for older adults, adults with disabilities and caregivers, at any income.
aging.next_step_extra: Press 1 for the Resource LINK. TTY users can call 711.

programs.name: North Dakota veterans: county and tribal veterans service officers for claims help
programs.organization: North Dakota Department of Veterans Affairs
programs.description: Free help with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits from county veterans service officers in every county and tribal veterans service officers for Fort Berthold, Lake Traverse, Spirit Lake, Standing Rock and Turtle Mountain. The department and the national service officers of AMVETS, the American Legion, DAV and VFW work at the Fargo VA Regional Office.
programs.next_step: Choose a county above for its county veterans service officer. Or call the North Dakota Department of Veterans Affairs at 701-239-7165. National service officers at the Fargo VA Regional Office: American Legion 701-451-4646, DAV 701-451-4636, VFW 701-451-4635.
constraints: Many rural county offices are open only a few days a month; check the hours on the county card and call ahead.
programs.phone_label: North Dakota Department of Veterans Affairs (701-239-7165)

programs.description: The Aging & Disability Resource LINK is the statewide starting point for older adults, adults with disabilities and caregivers: information and referral for help at home, meals, caregiver support, assisted living and other long-term services. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call 855-462-5465 and press 1 for the Resource LINK. TTY users can call 711.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (State Health Insurance Counseling, SHIC) for North Dakota
programs.organization: North Dakota Insurance Department, State Health Insurance Counseling (SHIC)
programs.description: Free Medicare counseling from North Dakota’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, SHIC, run by the Insurance Department with trained volunteer counselors.
programs.next_step: Call SHIC toll-free at 888-575-6611 (TDD 800-366-6888). For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

programs.name: North Dakota Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: North Dakota Health and Human Services: Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program; Vulnerable Adult Protective Services
programs.description: Advocacy for people living in nursing homes, basic care, assisted living and swing-bed hospitals. Vulnerable Adult Protective Services takes reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation of adults living in the community.
programs.next_step: Call the ombudsman at 701-328-4617, or 855-462-5465 and press 3. To report abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable adult, call 855-462-5465 and press 2 (weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.; messages can be left), or report online. In an emergency, call 911 first.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

programs.name: Free legal help for older North Dakotans
programs.organization: Legal Services of North Dakota; Dakota Plains Legal Services
programs.description: Legal Services of North Dakota gives free civil legal help to low-income and older North Dakotans, with a separate line for callers 60 and older. Dakota Plains Legal Services serves low-income people, older Americans and veterans, including in tribal courts.
programs.next_step: Age 60 and older: call Legal Services of North Dakota at 866-621-9886. Under 60: 800-634-5263.
constraints: Legal aid screens by income and case type.

programs.name: VA health care in North Dakota
programs.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Fargo VA Health Care System
programs.description: North Dakota veterans are served by the Fargo VA Health Care System: the Fargo VA Medical Center (2101 Elm Street North) and clinics including Bismarck, Grafton, Grand Forks, Jamestown and Minot.
programs.next_step: Call 701-239-3700 or toll-free 800-410-9723. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county veterans service officer for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 53 counties show a county veterans service officer (five through the Stark County office), the statewide Aging & Disability Resource LINK, the statewide long-term care ombudsman and a Center for Independent Living.
coverage_note: County veterans service officers come from the North Dakota Department of Veterans Affairs county pages. North Dakota has no Area Agencies on Aging; aging help, adult protective services and the ombudsman are reached through the statewide Resource LINK number. Independent living offices come from the ILRU national directory. Reviewed November 16, 2026. Contacts are not telephone-confirmed.
